hook.line: Don Hernando has been coming to the café for forty years, and he has a ranking for everything: the best coffee, the oldest street, the most expensive shop. To pick out the top one, Spanish takes the *más* you already know and puts *el* or *la* in front.
hook.es: Es el café más viejo del barrio.
hook.en: It's the oldest café in the neighbourhood.

examples.es: Bogotá es la ciudad más grande de Colombia.
examples.en: Bogotá is the biggest city in Colombia.

examples.es: Esta es la tienda más barata del centro.
examples.en: This is the cheapest shop in the centre.

examples.es: Es el mejor tinto del barrio.
examples.en: It's the best coffee in the neighbourhood.

examples.es: ¿Cuál es el plato más rico de la carta?
examples.en: What's the tastiest dish on the menu?

examples.es: Tomás es el mayor de la familia.
examples.en: Tomás is the oldest in the family.

examples.es: Esa chaqueta de cuero está carísima.
examples.en: That leather jacket is really expensive.

examples.es: Las arepas de Vale están riquísimas.

rule:
To say the most, put *el*, *la*, *los* or *las* before *más* and the adjective: *la ciudad más grande* is the biggest city. The article matches the noun, and the adjective agrees as usual.
For in, Spanish uses *de*: *la más grande de Colombia*, *el mejor del barrio* (*de* plus *el* is *del*). Never *en* here.
Best is just *mejor* with the article: *el mejor tinto*. The same goes for *mayor*: *el mayor* is the oldest.
The least works the same way, with *menos*: *la menos cara*.
For really, really, swap the last vowel for *ísimo*: *caro* becomes *carísimo*, *rico* becomes *riquísimo* (the c turns into qu to keep its sound). It agrees too: *carísima*, *riquísimas*. Nothing is being compared here; it just means very.
smallPrint: Teachers call *el más grande* the superlative, and *carísimo* the absolute superlative.
soundTip: In *ísimo* the stress jumps to the *í*: ca RÍ si mo, with an *í* like the ee in *see*.

readAndPick.es: Es la tienda más barata del centro.
options: It's the cheapest shop in the centre.
It's cheaper than the shop in the centre.
It's a very cheap shop.

readAndPick.es: Este café es más barato que el otro.
options: This coffee is the cheapest.
This coffee is cheaper than the other one.
This jacket is the most expensive.
This jacket is really expensive.

readAndPick.es: Es el mejor tinto del barrio.
options: It's better coffee than the neighbourhood's.
It's a good coffee in the neighbourhood.
It's the best coffee in the neighbourhood.

readAndPick.es: Simón es el menos tranquilo de la casa.
options: Simón is the least calm in the house.
Simón is the calmest in the house.

readAndPick.es: Bogotá es la ciudad más grande de Colombia.
options: Bogotá is a very big city in Colombia.
Bogotá is the biggest city in Colombia.
Bogotá is bigger than Colombia.

readAndPick.es: Tomás es el mayor de la familia.
options: Tomás is the youngest in the family.
Tomás is older than his family.
Tomás is the oldest in the family.
The arepas are absolutely delicious.
The arepas are the most delicious.
The arepas are more delicious.

readAndPick.es: Son las camisas más caras de la tienda.
options: The shirts in the shop are very expensive.
They're the most expensive shirts in the shop.
They're the cheapest shirts in the shop.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Es el café más viejo ___ barrio.* (*del* or *en el*) It's the oldest café in the neighbourhood.
yourTurn.answer: Es el café más viejo del barrio.
yourTurn.why: After the most, in is *de*, and *de* plus *el* is *del*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Es ___ tinto de Bogotá.* (*el más bueno* or *el mejor*) It's the best coffee in Bogotá.
yourTurn.answer: Es el mejor tinto de Bogotá.

yourTurn.prompt: Bogotá is the biggest city in Colombia.
yourTurn.answer: Bogotá es la ciudad más grande de Colombia.
yourTurn.why: *La ciudad más grande*, then *de* for in.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: This shop is the cheapest in the centre.
yourTurn.answer: Esta tienda es la más barata del centro.
yourTurn.why: *La más barata* agrees with *tienda*, and in the centre is *del centro*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: That leather jacket is really expensive. (use *ísimo*)
yourTurn.answer: Esa chaqueta de cuero está carísima.
accept: Esa chaqueta de cuero es carísima.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it the least: *Es la camisa más cara de la tienda.*
yourTurn.answer: Es la camisa menos cara de la tienda.
yourTurn.why: The least is *menos*; everything else stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Es la tienda más barata del barrio.*
yourTurn.answer: Son las tiendas más baratas del barrio.
yourTurn.why: *Son las tiendas*, and *baratas* agrees; *del barrio* stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it really, with *ísimo*: *El tinto está muy rico.*
yourTurn.why: *Rico* becomes *riquísimo*, and *muy* goes, because *ísimo* already means very.

pitfalls.wrong: Es el café más viejo en el barrio.
pitfalls.right: Es el café más viejo del barrio.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After the most, in is *de*: *del barrio*.

pitfalls.wrong: Es el más bueno tinto de Bogotá.
pitfalls.right: Es el mejor tinto de Bogotá.
pitfalls.why: Best has its own word: *el mejor*.

pitfalls.wrong: Bogotá es la más grande ciudad de Colombia.
pitfalls.right: Bogotá es la ciudad más grande de Colombia.
pitfalls.why: Close. The noun comes first, then *más* and the adjective.

personal: Name the best place you know for coffee or food, with *el mejor … de…* or *el más … de…*. Then describe something you love with an *ísimo* word.
